summary.plain: A detector combining a tank of liquid xenon (to catch a gamma ray) with a tracking chamber (to catch a positron) at the Paul Scherrer Institute, looking for both particles appearing together from a single muon decay.
summary.technical: Liquid xenon (LXe) scintillation calorimeter for the 52.8 MeV monochromatic gamma ray, combined with a drift chamber and scintillator timing counter positron spectrometer, on the PSI piE5 DC surface muon beamline. Operated 2009-2013; no separately sourced total LXe mass or chamber dimensions were fetched this session (left absent rather than guessed).

technology.quote: it consists of the µ+ beam, a thin stopping target, a thin-walled, superconducting magnet, a drift chamber array (DCH), scintillating timing counters (TC), and a liquid xenon calorimeter (LXe detector). ... the high intensity continuous surface µ+ beam (see Sect. 2.1) at PSI
technology.value: Liquid xenon calorimeter for the gamma ray, combined with a drift chamber and timing counter spectrometer for the positron, on the PSI DC muon beamline
